prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: The researchers used a retrospective observational cohort design involving patients from two hospitals that had round-the-clock CT scanning.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The study focused on adults aged 50 and older who received emergency CT scans for non-stroke reasons between January and December 2022.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Out of 6,535 eligible patients, 102 (1.6%) were found to have covert brain infarction on their CT scans.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: More than nine out of ten patients with covert brain infarction who were discharged from the emergency department received no changes to their medication or treatment plans.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Within one year of the initial visit, the group experienced 1 stroke or TIA, 4 heart attacks, 2 new diagnoses of atrial fibrillation, and 14 deaths.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The patients with covert brain infarction were mostly older adults with high rates of hypertension, dyslipidemia, atrial fibrillation, diabetes, and smoking.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The authors note that the current understanding of how common covert brain infarction is in the emergency department and how it is managed remains unclear.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The study concludes that more specific research and dedicated management pathways for this group of patients are needed.
facts.subject: humans
